transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-29
Time: 15:00 - 15:48 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lin (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Ethan Morales (CTO, CoralWave), Sara Kim (ML Lead), Liam Zhang (Infra)
---
Summary: quick discovery focused on model selection (open models), required context length, multilingual needs, and support for tool-calling / function calling. Discussed Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs and next steps to run benchmarks and share security docs.
---
Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Jordan from Redwood, with me is Priya our sales engineer. how are you all?
[00:05] Ethan: good, thanks, yeah excited to dig in. quick heads up, we only got about 45 mins so want to go through our constraints.
[00:10] Priya: great, high level — is CoralWave looking to evaluate hosted first or are you considering dedicated/private from day one?
[00:15] Sara: good question. we prefer hosted for speed to market but we have a parallel track for Dedicated or Private because of data residency and latency for some on-prem devices.
[00:20] Liam: also want to be clear on what "tool-calling" support looks like — we need function calling to orchestrate internal APIs and prompt grounded retrieval.
[00:28] Jordan: perfect, that's exactly what we'll cover. can you give a quick picture of your workload? context lengths, languages, QPS?
[00:35] Ethan: sure. main use case is agentic summarization for marine sensor logs plus a bilingual support chat (EN/ES). typical prompt + history ranges 3–5k tokens; occasionally need 30k+ for long document summarization. QPS is low initially (1–5 rps), but bursty.
[00:50] Priya: okay so two key axes: you need a model with long context (at least 32k ideally for those long docs) and good multilingual quality for Spanish, plus robust function-calling. also we should talk about embedding / retrieval for the summaries.
[01:05] Sara: yes embeddings are part of pipeline. what open models do you recommend? we've heard of Llama 3, Falcon, MPT, and some of the new 1T-context models, but not sure of tradeoffs.
[01:15] Priya: quick, high-level — Llama 3 variants tend to have strong instruction-following; Falcon is fast on inference and can be cheaper; MPT is flexible and has good long-context variants. there are also specialized long-context tuned models (some community forks). tradeoffs: accuracy vs cost vs context-support.
[01:30] Jordan: adding to that, Redwood's Hosted catalog includes tested profiles for several open models; we publish perf and cost estimates — we'll share a benchmark sheet after the call (link: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/coralwave).
[01:40] Ethan: nice. on context: you mentioned 32k — what about 100k or 1M context — are those realistic?
[01:45] Priya: realistic but depends. we support up to very large contexts via chunking + KV cache strategies. true 1M context tends to be experimental and model-dependent; often the practical approach is retrieval+local context + streaming summarization. for 30k+ we have tuned kernels and quantization profiles that keep latency reasonable.
[02:05] Liam: what about latency numbers? we care about p95 under bursts.
[02:08] Priya: p95 varies by model and deployment mode. Hosted (shared capacity) can hit roughly 200–600ms token latency for smaller contexts on optimized models; 32k contexts pushes to multiple seconds depending on tokens generated. Dedicated reserved GPU pools reduce interference and provide predictable latency — we can give model-specific p95 when we run your representative prompts.
[02:30] Sara: and cost? we compared hosted vs dedicated and saw big delta.
[02:33] Jordan: yes cost per token on Hosted is competitive for mixed workloads; Dedicated becomes economical at sustained high throughput because you reserve capacity. given your current QPS is low but bursty, a hybrid model (Hosted for dev + Dedicated for production bursts) is common.
[02:45] Ethan: ok that makes sense. another point: tool-calling — how do you handle secure API calls (we don't want model infra to have secrets)?
[02:50] Priya: function-calling is supported; for sensitive calls we recommend Redwood Private or Dedicated with VPC peering and KMS integration. we never store runtime secrets in logs; you can use customer-managed keys (HSM) if needed. we also have audit logs and RBAC in Console.
[03:05] Liam: good. are there SOC 2 / ISO docs we can share with our security team?
[03:08] Jordan: yes, we'll send SOC 2 and VPC/private deployment docs after the call.
[03:12] Ethan: great. on multilingual quality: do you have bench numbers for EN/ES? or fine-tuned models?
[03:17] Priya: we have internal evals; some models like Llama 3 perform well cross-lingual, others need fine-tuning. we can test your Spanish corpus as part of the benchmark run. please share a representative set (we'll treat it as confidential).
[03:30] Sara: will do.
[03:32] Jordan: another practical question — tool calling plus long context sometimes leads to memory blowups on GPU. do you support streaming and prefix caching?
[03:38] Priya: yes, streaming responses are standard; we also do KV cache and prefix caching which helps when user histories repeat. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization and batching settings to balance memory and latency.
[03:50] Ethan: what about model versioning and rollouts? we want canary tests and quick rollback.
[03:54] Priya: Console supports per-model rollouts, canary, A/B, and automatic fallback policies. that's identical across Hosted/Dedicated/Private so your engineers don't need to change code.
[04:05] Sara: helpful. any constraints for on-prem packages? we have some air-gapped requirements for a subset of data.
[04:10] Jordan: we offer Private deployments and an on-prem install for regulated workloads — it's heavier lift but supported. it includes audit logs, KMS, and offline deployment options.
[04:18] Liam: ok. how do we start the benchmarks? what do you need?
[04:21] Priya: ideally we need: (1) representative prompt set and long doc samples, (2) a short list of desired models to test, (3) target latency/cost goals. we'll run the tests on Hosted or a Dedicated pilot environment depending on which you prefer.
[04:35] Ethan: we'll put the prompt set together and send it. timeline — we want perf numbers within 2 weeks if possible.
[04:40] Jordan: sounds doable. Priya, can we allocate engineering time to run those?
[04:43] Priya: yes we'll run a baseline on Llama 3 (32k), Falcon (32k), and an MPT long-context variant; then adjust quantization. expect perf spreadsheet + recommendations in ~7–10 business days.
[04:58] Sara: nice. what about function-calling complexity — nested calls, multi-step tool orchestration?
[05:02] Priya: the runtime supports structured function outputs and tool chains; we also have guidance for prompt engineering to manage multi-step orchestration and state. for critical workflows we recommend a small state machine layer outside the model.
[05:15] Ethan: competitor question — we evaluate Bedrock and Anthropic. what's Redwood's edge?
[05:18] Jordan: quick answer: unified runtime + strong observability + cost controls. you get predictable serving, built-in caching, and rollout controls that many managed options don't offer. plus our model catalog has verified perf profiles for open models.
[05:32] Liam: can we get per-route token-level cost breakdowns?
[05:35] Priya: yes Console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route/model. very helpful to spot regressions.
[05:40] Ethan: ok. any gotchas on switching models mid-flight? we want fallback if a model is down.
[05:44] Priya: Redwood supports fallback policies — you can specify compatible variants and automatic routing by policy (latency, cost, region). that helps availability.
[05:55] Jordan: quick demo offer — we can do a follow-up demo focused on tool-calling and long-context behavior with your prompts.
[05:59] Sara: yes please, that would be useful.
[06:02] Ethan: agreed.
[06:04] Priya: we'll also need to scope a pilot — typical pilot is 2-week perf tests then 6-week integration.
[06:10] Jordan: i'll send suggested pilot scope in the follow-up email.
[06:13] Ethan: sweet. any immediate blockers? security is main one; also cost clarity.
[06:17] Jordan: we'll send SOC2 + VPC docs and a Hosted vs Dedicated cost sketch.
[06:22] Sara: side question: do you support multilingual embeddings? we use embeddings for retrieval and they must be consistent cross languages.
[06:28] Priya: yes we support multilingual embedding models; we'll include those results in the bench.
[06:34] Liam: about infra: if we go Dedicated, how does autoscaling work with reserved GPU pools?
[06:38] Priya: Dedicated has configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity; you reserve baseline and allow burst onto shared or extra nodes. SLA-backed uptime & latency goals possible in Dedicated contracts.
[06:50] Ethan: ok great. are there any limits on number of model versions?
[06:53] Jordan: not practically; Console supports versioning and pins.
[06:56] Sara: thanks, this is helpful.
[06:58] Jordan: quick recap — action items: we'll send benchmarks + pricing, SOC2 & VPC docs, and propose pilot scope. Priya will schedule a technical deep-dive to run benchmarks with your prompt set. Ethan will provide the prompt set and corpus. Sound right?
[07:12] Ethan: yep that matches.
[07:14] Liam: yep.
[07:16] Jordan: great. any closing questions?
[07:18] Sara: none from me.
[07:20] Ethan: no, thanks everyone.
[07:22] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up with the materials.
[07:25] (call ends)
